gapDrills.prompt: Bony tubercle on the anterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial condyle where the ILIOTIBIAL TRACT inserts:
gapDrills.detail: Explicitly named in Lab 5 syllabus ('Gerdy's tubercle — insertion of the iliotibial tract'). Sits lateral to tibial tuberosity on lateral condyle.

gapDrills.prompt: Which tendon uses the DORSAL TUBERCLE (Lister's tubercle) of the distal radius as a pulley (grooving just medial to it)?
gapDrills.detail: Lab 3 syllabus distal radius grooves: lateral to Lister's = ECRL & ECRB; immediately medial = Extensor pollicis longus (EPL); further medial = Extensor digitorum & extensor indicis.

gapDrills.prompt: Which two tendons groove the posterior border of the MEDIAL MALLEOLUS of the tibia ('Tom, Dick...')?
gapDrills.answer: Tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus
synonyms: tendons of tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus
tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus
gapDrills.detail: Lab 5 syllabus: posterior medial malleolus has groove for tibialis posterior & flexor digitorum longus tendons; further laterally on posterior distal tibia/talus/sustentaculum tali runs flexor hallucis longus.

gapDrills.prompt: Which muscle tendon occupies the deep oblique groove on the plantar surface of the CUBOID bone (and passes beneath the fibular trochlea of calcaneus)?
gapDrills.detail: Lab 5 syllabus highlights 'cuboid bone (groove for fibularis/peroneus longus muscle)' and calcaneus 'groove for fibularis longus tendon'.

gapDrills.prompt: Prominent lateral projection at the base of the 5th metatarsal (avulsed in inversion ankle injuries via fibularis brevis tendon):
gapDrills.detail: Insertion of fibularis (peroneus) brevis tendon; explicitly listed in Lab 5 practical knowledge.

gapDrills.prompt: Prominent medial landmark on the tarsal NAVICULAR bone (main insertion of tibialis posterior tendon):
gapDrills.detail: Palpable on medial border of foot anterior to sustentaculum tali; supports medial longitudinal arch.

gapDrills.prompt: Name the 2 LATERAL (radial) carpal bony prominences where the flexor retinaculum attaches (forming the lateral wall of the carpal tunnel):
gapDrills.answer: Tubercle of scaphoid and tubercle of trapezium
synonyms: tubercle of scaphoid and tubercle of trapezium
tuberosity of scaphoid and tuberosity of trapezium
gapDrills.detail: Flexor retinaculum spans from pisiform + hook of hamate (medial/ulnar) to tubercle of scaphoid + tubercle of trapezium (lateral/radial).

gapDrills.prompt: Name the 2 MEDIAL (ulnar) carpal bony landmarks where the flexor retinaculum attaches:
synonyms: pisiform bone and hook of hamate
gapDrills.detail: Hook (hamulus) of hamate and pisiform also bound Guyon's canal (ulnar nerve & artery).

gapDrills.prompt: List the 4 PROXIMAL row carpal bones from LATERAL (radial/thumb) to MEDIAL (ulnar):
gapDrills.detail: Radius carpal articular surface articulates directly with Scaphoid (lateral) and Lunate (medial); articular disc separates ulna from Triquetrum.

gapDrills.prompt: List the 4 DISTAL row carpal bones from LATERAL (thumb) to MEDIAL (5th digit):
gapDrills.detail: 'Trapezium sits under the Thumb' (1st CMC saddle joint); Capitate is the largest carpal bone.

gapDrills.prompt: Name the 3 structures injured in the classic 'Unhappy Triad' of the knee:
gapDrills.answer: Anterior cruciate ligament, tibial collateral ligament, medial meniscus
synonyms: acl, medial collateral ligament, medial meniscus
anterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament, medial meniscus
anterior cruciate ligament, tibial collateral ligament, medial meniscus
gapDrills.detail: Tibial (medial) collateral ligament is firmly fused to the MEDIAL meniscus (unlike fibular collateral ligament, which is separated from lateral meniscus by popliteus tendon).

gapDrills.prompt: Canal running anterolaterally ABOVE the occipital condyle that transmits Cranial Nerve XII:
gapDrills.detail: Transmits hypoglossal nerve (CN XII). Do not confuse with condylar canal POSTERIOR to occipital condyle (emissary vein)!

gapDrills.prompt: Canal piercing the root of the pterygoid process (foramen lacerum → pterygopalatine fossa) carrying the nerve of the pterygoid canal (Vidian nerve):
gapDrills.detail: Explicitly listed in Lab 9 practical structures ('pterygoid canal'): connects anterior wall of foramen lacerum to posterior wall of pterygopalatine fossa.

gapDrills.prompt: Cleft between greater wing of sphenoid and maxilla connecting the ORBIT with both the infratemporal and pterygopalatine fossae:
gapDrills.detail: Transmits infraorbital nerve & vessels (from CN V2), zygomatic nerve, & communication between inferior ophthalmic vein and pterygoid venous plexus.

gapDrills.prompt: Ragged opening at the apex of the petrous temporal bone closed by fibrocartilage in life (internal carotid artery passes ACROSS its upper aspect, greater petrosal nerve joins deep petrosal nerve here):
gapDrills.detail: Greater petrosal nerve (CN VII) + deep petrosal nerve (sympathetic) unite at foramen lacerum to enter pterygoid canal.

gapDrills.prompt: Which two pelvic ligaments convert the greater and lesser sciatic notches into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina?
gapDrills.detail: Sacrospinous attaches to ischial spine; sacrotuberous attaches to ischial tuberosity.

gapDrills.prompt: Name the 3 nerves directly contacting bone on the humerus from proximal to distal (Surgical neck → Radial groove → Medial epicondyle):
synonyms: axillary nerve, radial nerve, ulnar nerve
gapDrills.detail: Classic JUMC Lab 3 hook: Surgical neck → Axillary n.; Mid-shaft radial groove → Radial n.; Medial epicondyle → Ulnar n. (Distal supracondylar fracture risks Median n. & brachial a. anteriorly).

gapDrills.prompt: Through which skull opening does the VAGUS NERVE (CN X) exit the cranium (along with CN IX, CN XI, and internal jugular vein)?
gapDrills.detail: Watch out for the erroneous student-filled Lab 07 sheet: CN X exits via JUGULAR FORAMEN (posterior cranial fossa), NEVER superior orbital fissure!

gapDrills.prompt: What passes through Foramen Rotundum, Foramen Ovale, and Foramen Spinosum respectively (in order R → O → S)?
gapDrills.answer: Maxillary nerve (V2), mandibular nerve (V3), middle meningeal artery
synonyms: cn v2, cn v3, middle meningeal artery
maxillary bonery nerve (v2), mandibular nerve (v3), middle meningeal artery
maxillary bonery nerve , mandibular nerve (v3), middle meningeal artery
maxillary bonery nerve, mandibular nerve, middle meningeal artery
maxillary nerve (v2), mandibular nerve (v3), middle meningeal artery
maxillary nerve , mandibular nerve (v3), middle meningeal artery
maxillary nerve, mandibular nerve, middle meningeal artery
gapDrills.detail: Rotundum → V2 (to pterygopalatine fossa); Ovale → V3 + accessory meningeal a. + lesser petrosal n. (to infratemporal fossa); Spinosum → Middle meningeal vessels.

gapDrills.prompt: Which muscle originates via its straight head from the ANTERIOR INFERIOR ILIAC SPINE (and reflected head from supraacetabular groove)?
gapDrills.detail: ASIS = Sartorius (+ inguinal lig.); AIIS = Rectus femoris (+ iliofemoral lig.). High-yield hip bone confusion pair!

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Scapula specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Costal surface faces us (smooth subscapular fossa). Glenoid cavity and coracoid process face laterally (viewer's right).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Superior margin & suprascapular notch are superior; sharp inferior angle points downward.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Smooth concave subscapular fossa is anterior (faces ribs); dorsal spine is posterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Glenoid cavity and acromion face laterally (viewer's right); long straight medial border faces the vertebral column (viewer's left).
sidingRule.summary: Superior margin & suprascapular notch are superior; sharp inferior angle points downward. Smooth concave subscapular fossa is anterior (faces ribs); dorsal spine is posterior. Glenoid cavity and acromion face laterally (viewer's right); long straight medial border faces the vertebral column (viewer's left). → Confirms LEFT SCAPULA.

boneIdItems.trap: In anterior (costal) view: medial border is towards midline (viewer's left), and lateral glenoid cavity points towards the left shoulder (viewer's right) → Confirms LEFT SCAPULA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Scapula specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Dorsal surface faces us (prominent scapular spine visible). Acromion and glenoid are on the lateral side (viewer's left).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Supraspinatus fossa is superior; infraspinatus fossa is inferior; inferior angle points downward.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Spine of scapula is posterior (faces camera); costal surface is anterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Glenoid cavity and acromion are lateral (viewer's left); trigone of spine and medial border are medial (viewer's right).
sidingRule.summary: Supraspinatus fossa is superior; infraspinatus fossa is inferior; inferior angle points downward. Spine of scapula is posterior (faces camera); costal surface is anterior. Glenoid cavity and acromion are lateral (viewer's left); trigone of spine and medial border are medial (viewer's right). → Confirms LEFT SCAPULA.

boneIdItems.trap: In posterior (dorsal) view, looking at the back from behind: the lateral glenoid/acromion is on viewer's left (towards left arm), while medial vertebral margin is towards midline (viewer's right) → Confirms LEFT SCAPULA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Clavicle specimen LEFT or RIGHT?

sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Medial two-thirds is CONVEX anteriorly; lateral one-third is CONCAVE anteriorly.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Sternal end is quadrilateral and rounded (medial); acromial end is flattened (lateral).
sidingRule.summary: Superior surface is smooth; inferior surface has conoid tubercle, trapezoid line & subclavian groove. Medial two-thirds is CONVEX anteriorly; lateral one-third is CONCAVE anteriorly. Sternal end is quadrilateral and rounded (medial); acromial end is flattened (lateral). → Confirms LEFT CLAVICLE.

boneIdItems.trap: Sternal end medial (left), acromial end lateral (right), convex forward in medial 2/3 → LEFT CLAVICLE.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Clavicle specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Inferior surface is rough with conoid tubercle, trapezoid line, and sulcus for subclavius.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Inferior surface faces us (features conoid tubercle and subclavian groove).
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Conoid tubercle is POSTERIOR and inferior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Sternal end (medial) is on the right; acromial end with trapezoid line (lateral) is on the left.
sidingRule.summary: Inferior surface faces us (features conoid tubercle and subclavian groove). Conoid tubercle is POSTERIOR and inferior. Sternal end (medial) is on the right; acromial end with trapezoid line (lateral) is on the left. → Confirms LEFT CLAVICLE.

boneIdItems.trap: In inferior view, the posterio-inferior conoid tubercle sits along posterior border → LEFT CLAVICLE.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Humerus specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Head is proximal and faces medially; bicipital groove faces anteriorly; capitulum is lateral.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Rounded head is proximal; trochlea and capitulum are distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Intertubercular (bicipital) groove is anterior; deep olecranon fossa is posterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Articular head faces medially; larger medial epicondyle is medial.
sidingRule.summary: Rounded head is proximal; trochlea and capitulum are distal. Intertubercular (bicipital) groove is anterior; deep olecranon fossa is posterior. Articular head faces medially; larger medial epicondyle is medial. → Confirms LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Head medial, bicipital groove anterior → LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Humerus specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Head faces medially (viewer's left); lesser tubercle is anterior; greater tubercle is lateral (viewer's right).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Head is proximal/superior; surgical neck is inferior.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Lesser tubercle and intertubercular groove face anteriorly.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Articular head faces medially; greater tubercle sits laterally.
sidingRule.summary: Head is proximal/superior; surgical neck is inferior. Lesser tubercle and intertubercular groove face anteriorly. Articular head faces medially; greater tubercle sits laterally. → Confirms LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Head medial, lesser tubercle anterior → LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Humerus specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Medial epicondyle is on viewer's left; capitulum and lateral epicondyle on viewer's right; coronoid fossa anterior.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Shaft is proximal; articular condyles are distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Coronoid and radial fossae are anterior; deep olecranon fossa is posterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Medial epicondyle is large and medial; rounded capitulum is lateral.
sidingRule.summary: Shaft is proximal; articular condyles are distal. Coronoid and radial fossae are anterior; deep olecranon fossa is posterior. Medial epicondyle is large and medial; rounded capitulum is lateral. → Confirms LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Anterior view with medial epicondyle on left and capitulum on right → LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Humerus specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Deep olecranon fossa is posterior; ulnar nerve sulcus runs behind medial epicondyle on viewer's right.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Shaft is proximal; olecranon fossa is distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Deep triangular olecranon fossa is POSTERIOR.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Ulnar nerve sulcus grooves posterior surface of MEDIAL epicondyle (viewer's right in posterior view).
sidingRule.summary: Shaft is proximal; olecranon fossa is distal. Deep triangular olecranon fossa is POSTERIOR. Ulnar nerve sulcus grooves posterior surface of MEDIAL epicondyle (viewer's right in posterior view). → Confirms LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Posterior view with medial epicondyle on viewer's right → LEFT HUMERUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Radius specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Disc-like head is proximal; radial tuberosity points medially; pointed styloid process is lateral.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Circular head is proximal; expanded distal end with styloid process is distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Anterior surface of distal shaft is smooth and flat; posterior surface has Lister's dorsal tubercle.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Radial styloid process is LATERAL; ulnar notch and radial tuberosity are MEDIAL.
sidingRule.summary: Circular head is proximal; expanded distal end with styloid process is distal. Anterior surface of distal shaft is smooth and flat; posterior surface has Lister's dorsal tubercle. Radial styloid process is LATERAL; ulnar notch and radial tuberosity are MEDIAL. → Confirms LEFT RADIUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Head proximal, styloid lateral, ulnar notch medial → LEFT RADIUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Radius specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Smooth flat anterior surface; pointed styloid process on viewer's right (lateral); concave ulnar notch on viewer's left (medial).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Shaft is proximal; carpal articular facet is distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Flat, smooth distal anterior surface; extensor tendon grooves are posterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Styloid process is LATERAL (viewer's right); concave ulnar notch is MEDIAL (viewer's left).
sidingRule.summary: Shaft is proximal; carpal articular facet is distal. Flat, smooth distal anterior surface; extensor tendon grooves are posterior. Styloid process is LATERAL (viewer's right); concave ulnar notch is MEDIAL (viewer's left). → Confirms LEFT RADIUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Anterior surface facing us with styloid lateral (right) → LEFT RADIUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Radius specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Prominent dorsal (Lister's) tubercle is posterior; grooved for extensor pollicis longus tendon.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Shaft is proximal; carpal articular margin is distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Dorsal tubercle (Lister's tubercle) is distinctly POSTERIOR.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Styloid process is LATERAL; ulnar notch is MEDIAL.
sidingRule.summary: Shaft is proximal; carpal articular margin is distal. Dorsal tubercle (Lister's tubercle) is distinctly POSTERIOR. Styloid process is LATERAL; ulnar notch is MEDIAL. → Confirms LEFT RADIUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Posterior view with dorsal tubercle facing us → LEFT RADIUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Ulna specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Massive wrench-like proximal end; small head distally; sharp interosseous crest points laterally towards radius.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Olecranon and trochlear notch are proximal; small head and styloid process are distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Deep C-shaped trochlear notch faces ANTERIORLY.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Radial notch and sharp interosseous border are LATERAL; ulnar tuberosity is anterior/medial.
sidingRule.summary: Olecranon and trochlear notch are proximal; small head and styloid process are distal. Deep C-shaped trochlear notch faces ANTERIORLY. Radial notch and sharp interosseous border are LATERAL; ulnar tuberosity is anterior/medial. → Confirms LEFT ULNA.

boneIdItems.trap: Trochlear notch anterior, radial notch lateral → LEFT ULNA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Ulna specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Trochlear notch faces anteriorly; radial notch (shallow circular facet) is lateral on viewer's right.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Olecranon is proximal; shaft continues inferiorly.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: C-shaped trochlear notch faces anteriorly.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Radial notch for head of radius sits on LATERAL side of coronoid process.
sidingRule.summary: Olecranon is proximal; shaft continues inferiorly. C-shaped trochlear notch faces anteriorly. Radial notch for head of radius sits on LATERAL side of coronoid process. → Confirms LEFT ULNA.

boneIdItems.trap: Trochlear notch anterior, radial notch on lateral side → LEFT ULNA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Hip Bone specimen LEFT or RIGHT?

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Fan-shaped iliac blade is superior; obturator foramen & ischial tuberosity are inferior.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Pubis and pubic tubercle are ANTERIOR (viewer's right); greater sciatic notch and auricular surface are POSTERIOR (viewer's left).
sidingRule.medialLateral: Auricular surface and smooth internal iliac fossa face MEDIALLY; acetabulum faces laterally.
sidingRule.summary: Fan-shaped iliac blade is superior; obturator foramen & ischial tuberosity are inferior. Pubis and pubic tubercle are ANTERIOR (viewer's right); greater sciatic notch and auricular surface are POSTERIOR (viewer's left). Auricular surface and smooth internal iliac fossa face MEDIALLY; acetabulum faces laterally. → Confirms LEFT HIP BONE.

boneIdItems.trap: Internal (medial) view: facing the pelvic cavity with iliac blade superior, anterior pubis is on viewer's right and posterior sacral auricular surface is on viewer's left → Confirms LEFT HIP BONE.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Hip Bone specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Cup-like acetabulum faces laterally; ASIS & AIIS on viewer's left (anterior); ischial tuberosity on viewer's right (posterior).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Iliac crest is superior; ischial tuberosity and obturator foramen are inferior.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: ASIS and AIIS are ANTERIOR (viewer's left); PSIS, PIIS, and ischial tuberosity are POSTERIOR (viewer's right).
sidingRule.medialLateral: Acetabulum faces LATERALLY.
sidingRule.summary: Iliac crest is superior; ischial tuberosity and obturator foramen are inferior. ASIS and AIIS are ANTERIOR (viewer's left); PSIS, PIIS, and ischial tuberosity are POSTERIOR (viewer's right). Acetabulum faces LATERALLY. → Confirms LEFT HIP BONE.

boneIdItems.trap: Lateral (acetabular) view: looking at the left hip from the outside with iliac crest up, anterior spines are on viewer's left and posterior ischium is on viewer's right → Confirms LEFT HIP BONE.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Femur specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Head with fovea capitis projects medially (viewer's right); greater trochanter is lateral (viewer's left); intertrochanteric line is anterior.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Hemispherical head and neck are proximal/superior; shaft extends inferiorly.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Smooth shaft with flat intertrochanteric line is ANTERIOR; rough trochanteric crest is posterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Articular head projects MEDIALLY; greater trochanter sits LATERALLY.
sidingRule.summary: Hemispherical head and neck are proximal/superior; shaft extends inferiorly. Smooth shaft with flat intertrochanteric line is ANTERIOR; rough trochanteric crest is posterior. Articular head projects MEDIALLY; greater trochanter sits LATERALLY. → Confirms RIGHT FEMUR.

boneIdItems.trap: Anterior view with head pointing medially (right) and trochanter lateral (left) → RIGHT FEMUR.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Femur specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Posterior view: deep intercondylar fossa faces us; prominent adductor tubercle sits on medial epicondyle (viewer's left).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Shaft is proximal; condyles sit horizontally on tibial plateau.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Deep intercondylar fossa and flat popliteal surface are POSTERIOR; smooth patellar surface is anterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Medial condyle extends further back and carries adductor tubercle (viewer's left); lateral condyle has popliteal groove (viewer's right).
sidingRule.summary: Shaft is proximal; condyles sit horizontally on tibial plateau. Deep intercondylar fossa and flat popliteal surface are POSTERIOR; smooth patellar surface is anterior. Medial condyle extends further back and carries adductor tubercle (viewer's left); lateral condyle has popliteal groove (viewer's right). → Confirms RIGHT FEMUR.

boneIdItems.trap: Posterior view: with popliteal surface facing us, medial condyle/adductor tubercle is on viewer's left (towards midline) and lateral epicondyle is on viewer's right → Confirms RIGHT FEMUR.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Tibia specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Tibial tuberosity points anteriorly (up); medial condyle on viewer's left; lateral condyle (fibular facet) on viewer's right.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Plateau is proximal/superior; shaft extends downward.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Rough tibial tuberosity is ANTERIOR; posterior intercondylar area is posterior.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Medial condyle is larger and oval on viewer's left (medial); lateral condyle is circular and has fibular facet on viewer's right (lateral).
sidingRule.summary: Plateau is proximal/superior; shaft extends downward. Rough tibial tuberosity is ANTERIOR; posterior intercondylar area is posterior. Medial condyle is larger and oval on viewer's left (medial); lateral condyle is circular and has fibular facet on viewer's right (lateral). → Confirms RIGHT TIBIA.

boneIdItems.trap: Superior view of tibial plateau: with tibial tuberosity anterior (up), medial condyle is on viewer's left (towards midline) and lateral condyle is on viewer's right (towards fibula) → Confirms RIGHT TIBIA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Tibia specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Medial malleolus extends downward on the medial side (viewer's right); fibular notch sits laterally on opposite side (viewer's left).

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Shaft is proximal; quadrilateral inferior articular facet is distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Anterior margin is smooth; posterior margin is grooved for tibialis posterior and FDL tendons.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Medial malleolus is MEDIAL (viewer's right in anterior view); concave fibular notch is LATERAL (viewer's left in anterior view).
sidingRule.summary: Shaft is proximal; quadrilateral inferior articular facet is distal. Anterior margin is smooth; posterior margin is grooved for tibialis posterior and FDL tendons. Medial malleolus is MEDIAL (viewer's right in anterior view); concave fibular notch is LATERAL (viewer's left in anterior view). → Confirms RIGHT TIBIA.

boneIdItems.trap: Anterior view of distal tibia: looking from the front, medial malleolus is on viewer's right (towards midline) and fibular notch is on viewer's left → Confirms RIGHT TIBIA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Fibula specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Lateral malleolus distal; smooth triangular facet faces medially (towards talus); malleolar fossa is posterior.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Head with pointed apex is proximal; lateral malleolus is distal.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Deep triangular malleolar fossa is POSTERIOR to the articular facet.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Smooth triangular articular facet faces MEDIALLY towards talus.
sidingRule.summary: Head with pointed apex is proximal; lateral malleolus is distal. Deep triangular malleolar fossa is POSTERIOR to the articular facet. Smooth triangular articular facet faces MEDIALLY towards talus. → Confirms LEFT FIBULA.

boneIdItems.trap: Articular facet medial, malleolar fossa posterior → LEFT FIBULA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Calcaneus specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Calcaneal tuber is posterior (heel); sustentaculum tali projects medially as a horizontal shelf.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Talar articular facets are superior; rough calcaneal tuber touches the ground inferiorly.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Calcaneal tuber is POSTERIOR; cuboid articular facet is ANTERIOR.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Shelf-like sustentaculum tali projects MEDIALLY; peroneal trochlea is on lateral surface.
sidingRule.summary: Talar articular facets are superior; rough calcaneal tuber touches the ground inferiorly. Calcaneal tuber is POSTERIOR; cuboid articular facet is ANTERIOR. Shelf-like sustentaculum tali projects MEDIALLY; peroneal trochlea is on lateral surface. → Confirms RIGHT CALCANEUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Posterior tuber on right, medial shelf (sustentaculum tali) on bottom/medial side → RIGHT CALCANEUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Talus specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Rounded head faces anteriorly; convex trochlea superior; large triangular articular surface is on lateral side.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Convex pulley-like trochlea is superior; concave calcaneal facets are inferior.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Rounded head faces ANTERIORLY; posterior process with FHL groove is POSTERIOR.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Large triangular facet is LATERAL (fibula); small comma-shaped facet is MEDIAL (tibia).
sidingRule.summary: Convex pulley-like trochlea is superior; concave calcaneal facets are inferior. Rounded head faces ANTERIORLY; posterior process with FHL groove is POSTERIOR. Large triangular facet is LATERAL (fibula); small comma-shaped facet is MEDIAL (tibia). → Confirms LEFT TALUS.

boneIdItems.trap: Head anterior, large triangular facet lateral (viewer's right) → LEFT TALUS.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Typical Rib specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Head with articular facets is posterior; costal groove runs along the sharp inferior internal margin.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Superior border is thick and rounded; inferior border is sharp and contains the costal groove.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Head and tubercle are POSTERIOR (vertebral end); concave cup is ANTERIOR (sternal end).
sidingRule.medialLateral: Internal concave surface faces medially toward the lung; external surface is convex.
sidingRule.summary: Superior border is thick and rounded; inferior border is sharp and contains the costal groove. Head and tubercle are POSTERIOR (vertebral end); concave cup is ANTERIOR (sternal end). Internal concave surface faces medially toward the lung; external surface is convex. → Confirms RIGHT TYPICAL RIB.

boneIdItems.trap: Head posterior, costal groove inferior & internal → RIGHT RIB.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this 1st Rib specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Scalene tubercle is on inner border of superior surface; groove for subclavian vein is anterior to it, subclavian artery posterior.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Superior surface is grooved and marked by scalene tubercle; inferior surface is smooth with no costal groove.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Sternal end is ANTERIOR; head and neck are POSTERIOR.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Concave sharp margin is MEDIAL (internal); convex margin is LATERAL (external).
sidingRule.summary: Superior surface is grooved and marked by scalene tubercle; inferior surface is smooth with no costal groove. Sternal end is ANTERIOR; head and neck are POSTERIOR. Concave sharp margin is MEDIAL (internal); convex margin is LATERAL (external). → Confirms RIGHT 1ST RIB.

boneIdItems.trap: Head posterior, scalene tubercle on inner medial border, anterior groove for subclavian vein → RIGHT 1ST RIB.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Temporal Bone specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Lateral view of skull: face/orbit is on viewer's left (anterior), occiput on viewer's right (posterior). Zygomatic process points anteriorly, mastoid process posterior/inferior.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Flat thin squamous part is superior; conical mastoid process points inferiorly.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Zygomatic process projects ANTERIORLY (viewer's left); mastoid process is POSTERIOR (viewer's right).
sidingRule.medialLateral: External acoustic meatus (EAM) and squamous surface face LATERALLY (facing camera).
sidingRule.summary: Flat thin squamous part is superior; conical mastoid process points inferiorly. Zygomatic process projects ANTERIORLY (viewer's left); mastoid process is POSTERIOR (viewer's right). External acoustic meatus (EAM) and squamous surface face LATERALLY (facing camera). → Confirms LEFT TEMPORAL BONE.

boneIdItems.trap: Lateral view of the cranium: with face on viewer's left (anterior) and occiput on viewer's right (posterior), this lateral aspect faces the LEFT side of the head → Confirms LEFT TEMPORAL BONE.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Zygomatic Bone specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Lateral view of skull: face/orbit is on viewer's left (anterior), occiput on viewer's right (posterior). Frontal process points superiorly; temporal process extends posteriorly.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Pointed frontal process is SUPERIOR; maxilla-facing border is inferior and medial.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Smooth malar surface is ANTEROLATERAL; temporal process points POSTERIORLY (toward viewer's right).
sidingRule.medialLateral: Orbital surface is anteromedial; lateral malar surface faces viewer.
sidingRule.summary: Pointed frontal process is SUPERIOR; maxilla-facing border is inferior and medial. Smooth malar surface is ANTEROLATERAL; temporal process points POSTERIORLY (toward viewer's right). Orbital surface is anteromedial; lateral malar surface faces viewer. → Confirms LEFT ZYGOMATIC BONE.

boneIdItems.trap: Lateral view of skull: the face points to viewer's left (anterior) and occiput to viewer's right (posterior). You are viewing the LEFT cheek and zygomatic arch → Confirms LEFT ZYGOMATIC BONE.

boneIdItems.prompt: Is this Maxilla specimen LEFT or RIGHT?
boneIdItems.cue: Anterior facial view: note the pinned right maxilla (pins #2-5 on viewer's left: frontal process, zygomatic process, zygomaticoalveolar crest): frontal process points superiorly, teeth inferior, nasal notch medial.

sidingRule.superiorInferior: Frontal process is SUPERIOR; dental alveolar ridge is INFERIOR.
sidingRule.anteriorPosterior: Facial surface with canine fossa & infraorbital foramen faces ANTERIORLY; infratemporal surface faces posteriorly.
sidingRule.medialLateral: Nasal notch & piriform aperture border are MEDIAL (viewer's right for this right-side bone); zygomatic process is LATERAL (viewer's left).
sidingRule.summary: Frontal process is SUPERIOR; dental alveolar ridge is INFERIOR. Facial surface with canine fossa & infraorbital foramen faces ANTERIORLY; infratemporal surface faces posteriorly. Nasal notch & piriform aperture border are MEDIAL (viewer's right for this right-side bone); zygomatic process is LATERAL (viewer's left). → Confirms RIGHT MAXILLA.

boneIdItems.trap: Anterior view: with frontal process superior and teeth inferior, the patient's right maxilla sits on viewer's left (nasal notch medial, zygomatic process lateral) → Confirms RIGHT MAXILLA.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this specific vertebra at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Ring-shaped vertebra with NO body and NO spinous process. Features large concave kidney-shaped superior articular facets for occipital condyles (atlanto-occipital 'yes' joint).
boneIdItems.trap: Don't confuse with Axis (C2): Atlas has NO dens and NO body at all!

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this specific vertebra at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Pathognomonic upward-projecting tooth-like DENS (odontoid process) on the body. Large broad bifid spinous process. Serves as pivot for C1 rotation (atlanto-axial 'no' joint).
boneIdItems.trap: Dens instantly distinguishes C2 from every other vertebra in the human body.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this vertebra type at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: PATHOGNOMONIC TRANSVERSE FORAMINA in transverse processes (for vertebral artery). Triangular vertebral canal, small rectangular body with elevated lateral UNCI, and BIFID spinous process.
boneIdItems.trap: Transverse foramina are present ONLY in cervical vertebrae! If you see foramina in transverse processes, it is 100% CERVICAL.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this vertebra type at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: HEART-SHAPED vertebral body, circular vertebral foramen. Long slender spinous process sloping steeply downward. COSTAL FACETS on sides of body (for rib heads) and transverse processes (for rib tubercles).
boneIdItems.trap: Costal facets are unique to thoracic vertebrae! Lumbar vertebrae have NO costal facets.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this vertebra type at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: MASSIVE KIDNEY-SHAPED vertebral body (carries maximum axial weight). Triangular vertebral canal, short sturdy rectangular spinous process. Features MAMMILLARY PROCESSES on superior articular processes and ACCESSORY PROCESSES at base of transverse processes.
boneIdItems.trap: NO transverse foramina (not cervical) and NO costal facets (not thoracic). Mammillary processes are unique to lumbar vertebrae.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Triangular bone formed by fusion of 5 sacral vertebrae. Concave pelvic surface features the anterior sacral promontory, lateral sacral wings (alae), 4 pairs of anterior pelvic sacral foramina, and 4 transverse lines.
boneIdItems.trap: Pelvic surface is concave and smooth with large rounded pelvic sacral foramina.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bone / view at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Convex rough dorsal surface with 5 longitudinal crests: 1 MEDIAN sacral crest (fused spines), 2 INTERMEDIATE crests (fused articular processes), 2 LATERAL crests (fused transverse processes), 4 pairs of dorsal sacral foramina, and inferior SACRAL HIATUS flanked by cornua.
boneIdItems.trap: Sacral hiatus at S5 level is the clinical site for caudal epidural anesthesia.

boneIdItems.prompt: Which antebrachial bone is this?
boneIdItems.cue: Proximal end has a small cylindrical DISC-LIKE HEAD with fovea; distal end is expanded with a lateral styloid process and carpal articular facet.
boneIdItems.trap: Ulna has a massive wrench/hook (olecranon) proximally; Radius has a small circular wheel/disc head proximally.

boneIdItems.prompt: Which antebrachial bone is this?
boneIdItems.cue: Proximal end is massive and hook-shaped (olecranon & coronoid process grasping trochlea of humerus); distal end is small and tapered with a small rounded head and styloid process.
boneIdItems.trap: Radius is thicker distally; Ulna is much thicker proximally.

boneIdItems.prompt: Which leg (crural) bone is this?
boneIdItems.cue: Thick, massive weight-bearing bone. Sharp subcutaneous anterior border ('shin'), proximal expanded plateau, and prominent distal MEDIAL MALLEOLUS.
boneIdItems.trap: Tibia carries 100% of body weight from femur; Fibula carries 0% of body weight and does not touch the knee joint.

boneIdItems.prompt: Which leg (crural) bone is this?
boneIdItems.cue: Very slender, twisted non-weight-bearing strut. Bulbous proximal head with pointed styloid apex; distal end forms the flattened LATERAL MALLEOLUS with malleolar fossa.
boneIdItems.trap: Much more slender than Tibia; articulates laterally with tibia at both ends but NOT with femur.

boneIdItems.prompt: Which long bone is this?
boneIdItems.cue: Smooth hemispherical head sitting almost directly on anatomical neck; GREATER and LESSER TUBERCLES separated by deep intertubercular (bicipital) groove.
boneIdItems.trap: Femur head has a distinct pit (fovea capitis) and a long, sharply angled neck (~125°); Humerus has NO fovea capitis and has greater/lesser TUBERCLES (not trochanters).

boneIdItems.prompt: Which long bone is this?
boneIdItems.cue: Massive hemispherical head with distinct central FOVEA CAPITIS, long cylindrical neck (~125° angle of inclination), massive GREATER TROCHANTER and lesser trochanter.
boneIdItems.trap: Trochanters belong strictly to Femur! Tubercles belong to Humerus. Linea aspera on posterior shaft is pathognomonic of Femur.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Double-curved elongated S-shaped bone. Bulbous rounded medial sternal end, flattened lateral acromial end, smooth superior surface.
boneIdItems.trap: Rib has a single C-shaped curvature; Clavicle has a double S-shaped curvature. Clavicle has NO costal groove.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Single-curved flat C-shaped bone. Posterior vertebral end has head with two articular demifacets, neck, and tubercle; inferior border has deep costal groove on internal side.
boneIdItems.trap: Clavicle is S-shaped with two distinct curvatures; Rib is a flat C-shaped arc with costal groove.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this specific rib at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: SHORTEST, BROADEST, and MOST CURVED of all ribs. Lies almost horizontally. Features scalene tubercle on inner margin flanked by anterior sulcus for subclavian vein and posterior sulcus for subclavian artery.
boneIdItems.trap: Lacks a costal groove; superior surface is marked by neurovascular grooves; 2nd rib is twice as long.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this specific rib at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Twice as long as 1st rib. Features a prominent rough TUBEROSITY FOR SERRATUS ANTERIOR (origin of 1st and 2nd digitation of serratus anterior) on its external surface.
boneIdItems.trap: Pathognomonic tuberosity for serratus anterior near the middle of its outer surface.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this thoracic wall bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Elongated flat 'dagger-shaped' bone in anterior thoracic midline. Composed of manubrium, body (mesosternum), and inferior xiphoid process. Sternal angle (angle of Louis) is at T4/T5 disc level (2nd rib landmark).
boneIdItems.trap: Costal notches along lateral margins articulate with true ribs 1–7.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this upper sternal segment at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Thick quadrilateral / trapezoidal superior part of sternum. Superior border features central JUGULAR (suprasternal) NOTCH flanked by bilateral oval CLAVICULAR NOTCHES for sternoclavicular (SC) joints.
boneIdItems.trap: Lateral border has synchondrosis facet for 1st rib cartilage; articulates inferiorly at sternal angle.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this pectoral girdle bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Flat triangular blade on posterolateral thoracic wall. Easily identified by the prominent DORSAL SPINE terminating laterally in the flattened ACROMION, and the anterior beak-like CORACOID PROCESS.
boneIdItems.trap: Shallow pear-shaped glenoid cavity articulates with humerus; hip bone has deep hemispherical acetabulum.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this pelvic girdle bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Large irregular bone formed by fusion of ilium, ischium, and pubis. Identified by the massive cup-shaped ACETABULUM (hip socket), huge OBTURATOR FORAMEN, and GREATER SCIATIC NOTCH.
boneIdItems.trap: Much thicker and heavier than scapula; forms pelvic ring with sacrum.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this carpal bone in the proximal row (radial side):
boneIdItems.cue: Largest bone of proximal carpal row, on radial side. Boat-shaped (navicular) with a prominent palpable tubercle on palmar surface. Articulates with radius. Most commonly fractured carpal bone (snuffbox tenderness; risk of avascular necrosis).
boneIdItems.trap: Mnemonics: 'Some Lovers Try Positions...' (Scaphoid is first, radial side of proximal row).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this crescent-shaped carpal bone articulating with the radius:
boneIdItems.cue: Crescent / moon-shaped proximal carpal bone between scaphoid and triquetrum. Articulates with radius. Most commonly DISLOCATED carpal bone (displaces anteriorly into carpal tunnel, compressing median nerve).
boneIdItems.trap: Lunate = lunar / moon shape. Sits right in the midline of proximal row.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this carpal bone underlying the pisiform:
boneIdItems.cue: Pyramidal three-cornered bone medial to lunate on ulnar side of proximal row. Features an isolated oval articular facet on its palmar surface for the pisiform.
boneIdItems.trap: Pisiform sits directly ON TOP of the triquetrum's palmar surface.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this pea-shaped sesamoid carpal bone:
boneIdItems.cue: Small pea-shaped sesamoid bone located entirely inside the flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU) tendon on palmar surface of triquetrum. Forms the medial pillar of the carpal tunnel.
boneIdItems.trap: Pisiform is the ONLY sesamoid bone of the carpus and does not participate in wrist joint articulation.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this carpal bone with the saddle facet for the thumb:
boneIdItems.cue: Most lateral bone of the distal carpal row. Features a pathognomonic SADDLE-SHAPED articular facet for the base of the 1st metacarpal (thumb CMC joint allowing opposition) and an anterior tubercle.
boneIdItems.trap: Trapezium = 'under the thumb'. Trapezoid is inside (under index finger).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this boot-shaped carpal bone under the index finger:
boneIdItems.cue: Smallest bone in the distal carpal row. Boot / shoe-shaped, articulates distally with the 2nd metacarpal base.
boneIdItems.trap: TrapeziUM is near the thUMB; TrapezoID is InsiDe.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this largest carpal bone sitting in the center of the wrist:
boneIdItems.cue: LARGEST carpal bone, sitting in the anatomical center of the wrist. Features a rounded head articulating with scaphoid and lunate, articulating distally mainly with 3rd metacarpal (longitudinal axis of hand).
boneIdItems.trap: Capitate = 'head' / largest keystone carpal.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this carpal bone with a prominent hook (hamulus):
boneIdItems.cue: Wedge-shaped distal carpal bone on the ulnar side. Instantly recognized by its hook-like anterior projection: the HAMULUS (hook of hamate). Forms medial boundary of carpal tunnel and lateral wall of Guyon's canal (ulnar nerve).
boneIdItems.trap: Hook of hamate fracture can injure the deep motor branch of ulnar nerve.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this tarsal bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: LARGEST tarsal bone (heel bone). Features massive posterior calcaneal tuber (insertion of Achilles tendon), three talar articular facets, and the medial horizontal shelf: SUSTENTACULUM TALI.
boneIdItems.trap: Sustentaculum tali is grooved inferiorly by flexor hallucis longus (FHL) tendon.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this tarsal bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Second largest tarsal bone. Transmits 100% of body weight from leg to foot. HAS NO MUSCLE OR TENDON INSERTIONS! Composed of body with convex pulley-like TROCHLEA, neck, and rounded anterior head.
boneIdItems.trap: Talus is the only tarsal bone articulating directly with the crural bones (tibia and fibula).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this boat-shaped midfoot tarsal bone:
boneIdItems.cue: Boat-shaped bone on medial side of midfoot between talar head and the 3 cuneiforms. Features a prominent, palpable medial NAVICULAR TUBEROSITY (insertion of TIBIALIS POSTERIOR tendon; keystone of medial longitudinal arch).
boneIdItems.trap: Navicular = boat (like scaphoid). Sits on MEDIAL side of foot between talus and 3 cuneiforms.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this cube-shaped lateral midfoot tarsal bone:
boneIdItems.cue: Cube-shaped bone on the LATERAL side of midfoot, articulating proximally with calcaneus and distally with 4th and 5th metatarsals. Plantar surface has a deep oblique GROOVE FOR FIBULARIS (PERONEUS) LONGUS TENDON.
boneIdItems.trap: Cuboid sits on LATERAL side in front of calcaneus; Navicular sits on MEDIAL side in front of talus.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this largest cuneiform bone (medial border of foot):
boneIdItems.cue: LARGEST of the three cuneiform bones. Sits on the medial border of the foot, articulating distally with the base of the 1st metatarsal (tibialis anterior and fibularis longus insert on its anteroinferior surface).
boneIdItems.trap: Medial cuneiform is largest; intermediate cuneiform is smallest.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this smallest cuneiform bone recessed between medial & lateral cuneiforms:
boneIdItems.cue: SMALLEST of the three cuneiforms. Wedge-shaped with apex pointing plantarward. Recessed proximally between medial and lateral cuneiforms, locking the 2nd metatarsal base into a mortise ('mortise of Lisfranc joint').
boneIdItems.trap: Locks 2nd metatarsal base in place like a tenon and mortise.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this cuneiform bone articulating with the cuboid:
boneIdItems.cue: Intermediate in size, wedge-shaped with base dorsal. Sits between intermediate cuneiform and cuboid, articulating distally with the base of the 3rd metatarsal.
boneIdItems.trap: Articulates laterally with the cuboid bone.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this butterfly-shaped skull base bone:
boneIdItems.cue: Butterfly / bat-shaped keystone bone of the skull base. Greater wings, lesser wings, pterygoid processes, and central body with sella turcica (hypophysial fossa) housing the pituitary gland.
boneIdItems.trap: Forms central part of middle cranial fossa; transmits CN II (optic canal), CN III, IV, V1, VI (SOF), V2 (foramen rotundum), V3 (foramen ovale).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bone housing the auditory and vestibular apparatus:
boneIdItems.cue: Houses the middle and inner ear. Composed of squamous part, petrous part (pyramid with arcuate eminence & trigeminal impression), tympanic part (surrounds EAM), and styloid/mastoid processes.
boneIdItems.trap: Features mandibular fossa for TMJ, external & internal acoustic meati, carotid canal, and stylomastoid foramen (CN VII exit).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this posterior cranial fossa & cranial base bone:
boneIdItems.cue: Forms the posterior cranial fossa and external cranial base. Features the massive FORAMEN MAGNUM, paired occipital condyles (atlanto-occipital joint), pharyngeal tubercle on basilar part, and external occipital protuberance (inion).
boneIdItems.trap: Occipital condyles articulate directly with the superior articular facets of the Atlas (C1).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this lower jaw bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Strongest, largest, and ONLY mobile bone of the facial skeleton (viscerocranium). Horseshoe-shaped horizontal body and two vertical rami. Coronoid process anteriorly, condylar process (head of mandible) posteriorly, mental foramen, and mandibular canal with lingula.
boneIdItems.trap: Articulates with temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint (TMJ).

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this non-articulating U-shaped neck bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: U-shaped bone in the anterior neck at C3 level. DOES NOT ARTICULATE WITH ANY OTHER BONE (suspended by muscles and stylohyoid ligament). Composed of a central body, bilateral GREATER HORNS (cornua), and small upward LESSER HORNS.
boneIdItems.trap: Serves as attachment site for suprahyoid and infrahyoid strap muscles and tongue musculature.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this cranial vault bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Quadrilateral curved bone forming the vertex and lateral sides of the cranial vault. Prominent central parietal tuber (eminence); articulates with frontal bone at coronal suture and occipital bone at lambdoid suture.
boneIdItems.trap: Grooved internally by anterior and posterior branches of the middle meningeal artery.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this anterior neurocranium bone at a glance:
boneIdItems.cue: Shell-shaped bone forming forehead and roofs of orbits. Features smooth median GLABELLA, prominent SUPERCILIARY ARCHES, and sharp SUPRAORBITAL MARGINS with supraorbital notch/foramen (for CN V1 branches).
boneIdItems.trap: Contains the bilateral frontal paranasal sinuses draining into the middle nasal meatus.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bony structure forming the roof of the oral cavity:
boneIdItems.cue: Bony roof of the mouth and floor of the nasal cavity. Formed anterior 2/3 by PALATINE PROCESSES OF MAXILLAE and posterior 1/3 by HORIZONTAL PLATES OF PALATINE BONES, joined by median and transverse palatine sutures.
boneIdItems.trap: Features incisive canal anteriorly and greater/lesser palatine foramina posterolaterally.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify the deep orbital bones forming the Superior Orbital Fissure:
boneIdItems.cue: Posterior wall of orbit. SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE separates the upper LESSER WING from the lower GREATER WING of the sphenoid bone. Transmits CN III, IV, V1 (lacrimal, frontal, nasociliary), VI, and superior ophthalmic vein.
boneIdItems.trap: Lesser wing forms upper margin of SOF and optic canal; Greater wing forms lower margin.

boneIdItems.prompt: Identify this bone from its internal posterior symphyseal view:
boneIdItems.cue: Internal surface of mandibular symphysis (chin). Features bilateral oval DIGASTRIC FOSSAE (anterior belly of digastric), MENTAL SPINES / genial tubercles (genioglossus & geniohyoid), SUBLINGUAL FOSSA superiorly, and MYLOHYOID LINE.
boneIdItems.trap: Genial tubercles / mental spines project from internal midline; digastric fossa sits along lower border.
